text: In the study by Mann et al. (lying) both the samples of video clips and of police officers were
obtained by opportunity sampling.

parts.text: What is meant by a ‘repeated measures design’?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one advantage of a repeated measures design in this study.

text: The study by Loftus and Pickrell (false memories) used a repeated measures design.

parts.text:
Suggest why it was important that both Group 2 and Group 1 (the experimental group) had a
wide range of occupations and education.

text: In the study by Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test) a varied group of participants was used in Group 2
(the normal adults).

Explain the Oedipus complex using little Hans as an example. [4]
From the study by Dement and Kleitman:
Describe the findings about the relationship between dream content and eye movement. [4]

parts.text: Explain why this study was a laboratory experiment.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why this study may have low validity.

text: The study by Maguire et al. (taxi drivers) was a laboratory experiment. This method typically has
good reliability but sometimes has low validity.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe one aim of the study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Using results from the study, explain whether the aim you have described in (a) was
supported.

text: From the study by Demattè et al. (smells and facial attractiveness):
Rosenhan (sane in insane places) suggested that decisions about sanity are based on the beliefs
of psychiatrists not the characteristics displayed by patients.
Describe two ways that the results show whether this suggestion is true. [4]

questionnaire.
